_comment: Character traits (scripts/sim/traits.gd Traits; DESIGN_LIVING_WORLD.md Characters and traits): CK3-style, one system for every character. The player's CEO gets theirs from the backstory start (data/backstories.json); every paper shipping firm's CEO gets one to three at random. skills: added to the character's five skills (Seamanship, Finance, Negotiation, Engineering, Leadership; from 0, no upper cap). effects: what a CEO's traits do for the whole company, summed over their traits: price (x sale prices), fuel (less fuel burnt), wear (less maintenance lost at sea), breakdowns (fewer), wages (less crew pay), interest (less loan interest), fees (less port fees and tolls: to come). ai: how a paper firm's CEO with the trait runs it (margin: the gain over freight it sails for, x the firm's; to come). opposites can't be held together. story: the sentence a backstory ends with for the trait, {name} the CEO's name.

traits.name: Shrewd
traits.text: Sees the margin in every deal.
traits.story: {name} has never signed a contract without reading it twice, and it shows in the prices.

traits.name: Thrifty
traits.text: Runs a tight ship: fuel and wages watched.
traits.story: {name} counts every ton of bunker fuel and every overtime hour, and the books are the better for it.

traits.name: Engineer
traits.story: {name} still goes down to the engine room on every visit, and the ships wear slower for it.

traits.name: Ex-Navy
traits.text: Years in the service: discipline aboard, and friends in uniform.
traits.story: {name} left the navy a commander, and crews that sail for {name} find the standards came along.

traits.name: Gambler
traits.text: Sails for the big score and skimps on the small stuff.
traits.story: {name} will take the thin cargo to the far port on a hunch, and sometimes the hunch pays.

traits.name: Cautious
traits.text: Never the first to move, never the one caught out.
traits.story: {name} would rather miss a deal than lose a ship, and has lost none yet.

traits.name: Charismatic
traits.text: People want to work for them, and to deal with them.
traits.story: Dockers, brokers and bankers all seem to end up on {name}'s side of the table.

traits.name: Old Salt
traits.text: Forty years at sea before the office.
traits.story: {name} went to sea at sixteen and knows every shortcut the charts don't show.

traits.name: Bookkeeper
traits.text: An accountant first: banks trust the figures.
traits.story: {name} came up through the counting house, and the bank lends to {name} on better terms than most.

traits.name: Reckless
traits.story: {name} runs ships hard and takes the repair bills as they come.

traits.name: Well-connected
traits.story: There isn't a harbourmaster between here and the far side of the world who hasn't had a drink with {name}.

traits.name: Naive
traits.text: New to all this; brokers see them coming.
traits.story: {name} has a lot to learn about freight, and the brokers know it.

traits.name: Lavish
traits.text: Spends freely: happy crews, thin margins.
traits.story: {name} believes a good crew is worth paying for, and pays.

traits.name: Abrasive
traits.story: {name} is not easy to work for, which the turnover shows, but the numbers are never wrong.

traits.name: Landlubber
traits.text: Never been to sea; the office is the ship.
traits.story: {name} gets seasick on the ferry, and leaves the sailing to the captains.

traits.name: Scholar
traits.text: Reads the research before the rivals do.
traits.story: {name} keeps up with every journal and trial, and the fleet is the first to try what works.
